common: A Whiter Shade of Pale Rose
latin: Rosa A WHITER SHADE OF PALE ('Peafanfare')
visual: Compact upright Hybrid Tea rose with elegant scrolled buds opening into large, very pale blush-pink to near-white double flowers; strongly fragrant against glossy dark green foliage.
water: Water deeply during prolonged dry periods, especially while establishing and when grown in containers; avoid repeatedly wetting the foliage.
soilWarning: No waterlogging; renew old rose soil
prune: Prune as a Hybrid Tea in late winter or early spring, removing dead, weak or crossing growth and shortening strong stems; deadhead regularly to encourage repeat flowering.
toxicity: Low hazard if eaten; the thorny stems are sharp and can injure skin, so wear gloves when handling.
resilience: Hardy, repeat-flowering and noted for good disease resistance; established plants are reliable across most UK gardens.
uses: Rose beds, mixed borders, cottage gardens, courtyards, large containers and cut flowers
